subject: chemistry-2
question: Normal arterial blood is maintained in the pH range 7.35 to 7.45. Which description of that range is accurate?

options.text: Strongly acidic, far below the neutral point of water
Slightly alkaline, just above the neutral point of water
Strongly alkaline, near the upper end of the pH scale
Exactly neutral, identical to pure water at 25 °C

explanation:
Pure water at 25 °C is neutral at pH 7, so a range centered near 7.4 lies slightly above neutral and is correctly described as slightly alkaline. It is not strongly alkaline; solutions of strong bases occupy pH values near 12 to 14. Recognizing that blood sits only a few tenths of a unit above neutral explains why deviations of even 0.1 unit are reported as clinically meaningful.

ELI-10: On the 0 to 14 scale, 7 marks the point where hydronium and hydroxide are equal. Blood at 7.4 sits just past that point on the basic side, not far out toward the strongly basic end. In concentration terms, 7.4 means about 4 × 10^-8 mol/L hydronium versus 1 × 10^-7 mol/L in neutral water, so blood holds roughly two and a half times less hydronium than plain water. 'Slightly alkaline' is the precise description.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
